current_episode.title: Darren Prince:From Addiction to Representing Legends Like Magic Johnson & Muhammad Ali |Sean Callagy

guest.bio_context: Darren Prince started in the baseball card business at age 14 and was making half a million dollars annually by his early twenties. He transitioned into booking autograph signings for celebrities like Muhammad Ali, Magic Johnson, and Pamela Anderson, but faced legal challenges including a felony charge related to autograph authentication. After 18 years of sobriety, he built Prince Martin Group into a major celebrity representation agency representing clients including Magic Johnson, David Goggins, and Muhammad Ali. He authored the international bestseller 'Aiming High,' which documents his journey through addiction and recovery, and founded the Aiming High Foundation to serve people struggling with substance abuse and veterans.

pending_qa.q: How does assessing whether people are net givers versus net takers impact personal and professional relationships?
pending_qa.r: Net givers are those who consistently contribute more value to relationships and communities than they extract, while net takers deplete energy through one-directional benefit. The integrity of a relationship depends on this pattern assessment: someone might give 99 to 1 occasionally, but when energy consistently flows outward without reciprocal contribution, the relationship becomes unsustainable. Identifying net givers versus takers helps determine who should remain in one's inner circle and who shouldn't, preventing unnecessary pain and heartache.
